ai.title: CAO 10-2020: Seizure and Forfeiture Proceedings and Appeals Process
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang CAO No. 10-2020 ang procedure ng Bureau of Customs sa seizure at forfeiture ng mga properties na lumabag sa CMTA, kasama ang settlement, appeals at automatic review. Ipinatutupad nito ang Secs. 1113 hanggang 1117 at 1119 hanggang 1125 (Chapter 4) at Secs. 1126 hanggang 1128 (Chapter 5) ng Title XI ng RA 10863 o CMTA.

🔍 Breakdown: Secs. 1 at 2: scope at objectives. Sec. 3: definitions. Sec. 4: properties subject to seizure at forfeiture, at conditions for forfeiture. Sec. 5: seizure sa power to inspect and visit (15-day proof). Sec. 6: issuance at service ng WSD. Secs. 7 at 8: custody ng seized goods. Sec. 9: forfeiture proceedings. Secs. 10 hanggang 13: pleadings, hearing officer, hearing proper at prohibited motions. Sec. 14: remedies (quashal, settlement, decision). Sec. 15: referral sa IAS. Secs. 16 at 17: appeal at automatic review. Secs. 18 hanggang 23: penal, transitory, periodic review, repealing, separability at effectivity.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Parang roadmap ng isang kaso: may nakitang violation, mag-iissue ng WSD, may hearing, may Decision ang District Collector, tapos appeal o automatic review hanggang Secretary of Finance at Court of Tax Appeals. May mga daan din para makuha pa rin ang goods: quashal ng WSD, o settlement by fine o redemption.

📦 Halimbawa: May shipment na sa physical examination ay mas marami ang goods kaysa sa idineklara. Nag-issue ang District Collector ng WSD, na-seize ang goods at dinala sa ACDD. Nag-hearing, nagsumite ng Position Paper ang importer, at nag-offer ng settlement. Dahil walang Fraud at hindi absolutely prohibited ang goods, puwedeng pag-aralan ang settlement, basta hindi lalampas sa 30% ang discrepancy kung fine ang gagamitin.

⭐ Bakit Mahalaga Ito? Dito nakasalalay ang karapatan ng importer at ang interes ng gobyerno. Mahigpit ang mga deadlines at bawal ang maraming motions, kaya ang customs broker at importer ay dapat marunong sa tamang proseso.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: 15 araw para sa proof of payment (Sec. 5.1), 3 working days sa service ng WSD (Sec. 6.5), 30% fine at 100% redemption ng Landed Cost (Sec. 14.4), 30% surcharge sa undeclared baggage (Sec. 14.2), 15 araw sa appeal at 5 araw kung perishable (Sec. 16.1), at Php 10,000,000.00 FOB o FCA value para sa review ng Secretary of Finance (Sec. 17.2).

🎯 Board Exam Tip: Tandaan ang mga periods at percentages, ang pagkakaiba ng seizure at forfeiture, at ang mga kundisyon ng settlement (walang Fraud, hindi absolutely prohibited, hindi labag sa batas ang release). Kilalanin din ang anim na prohibited motions sa Sec. 13.

❓ Madalas Malito ang Students: Pareho ba ang seizure at forfeiture? Hindi. Ang seizure ay ang pagkuha o pag-hold sa goods sa bisa ng WSD (Sec. 3.22). Ang forfeiture ay ang pagkuha ng gobyerno ng ownership bilang resulta ng forfeiture proceedings (Sec. 3.11).

🔗 Related Topics: CMTA Title XI Chapters 4 at 5, Sec. 224 ng CMTA (inspect and visit), CAO 7-2019 (Alert Order), CAO 1-2020 (fines at surcharges), CAO 1-2017 (baggage), CMO 29-1997 (service ng notices).

paragraphs.text: This CAO implements Sections 1113 to 1117, Sections 1119 to 1125, Chapter 4 and Sections 1126 to 1128, Chapter 5 of Title XI and other relevant provisions of Republic Act No. 10863, otherwise known as the Customs Modernization and Tariff Act (CMTA).

ai.title: Legal Basis ng CAO
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Sinasabi dito kung saang batas nakabase ang CAO: Title XI ng CMTA (RA 10863), partikular ang seizure at forfeiture sa Chapter 4 at ang appeals sa Chapter 5.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ang CAO na ito ay 'implementing rules' lang. Ang tunay na pinagmumulan ng kapangyarihan ay ang CMTA mismo.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Kapag may conflict, ang CMTA ang mananaig. Tandaan ang range ng sections na binanggit dito.

paragraphs.text: This CAO covers all properties subject to seizure and forfeiture as enumerated under Section 1113 found to be in violation of the CMTA.

ai.title: Scope ng CAO
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Saklaw ng CAO ang lahat ng properties na puwedeng i-seize at i-forfeit ayon sa listahan ng Sec. 1113 ng CMTA, kapag may nakitang violation.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kung nasa listahan ng Sec. 1113 ang property at lumabag sa CMTA, sakop ito ng procedure ng CAO na ito.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang listahan ng properties ay inilatag sa Sec. 4.1 ng CAO: goods, vehicle/vessel/aircraft, cargo/stores, at packages.

paragraphs.text: Alert Order — shall refer to a written order issued by the Commissioner, District Collector, or other customs officers authorized in writing by the Commissioner after the Lodgement of goods declaration and before their actual release from customs custody, on the basis of derogatory information stated in this CAO regarding possible non-compliance with the CMTA and other laws, rules and regulations enforced by Customs.

ai.title: Alert Order
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Written order na nagho-hold ng release ng goods kahit na-lodge na ang goods declaration, dahil may derogatory information tungkol sa posibleng non-compliance.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi pa ito seizure. Hold muna habang sinusuri kung may violation. Puwedeng manggaling sa Commissioner, District Collector, o authorized customs officer na may written authority.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang timing: pagkatapos ng lodgement at bago ang actual release. Ang mas detalyadong rules ay nasa CAO 7-2019.

paragraphs.text: Coastwise Trade — shall refer to the business of transferring either merchandise or passengers between two seaports in the Philippines.

ai.title: Coastwise Trade
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Negosyo ng paglipat ng merchandise o pasahero sa pagitan ng dalawang seaport sa Pilipinas.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Domestic shipping lang ito, hindi international.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Mahalaga ito sa Sec. 4.1.2(c): ang vessel sa coastwise trade na may foreign goods na hindi properly entered ay puwedeng i-seize.

paragraphs.text: Commercial Quantity — shall refer to the quantity for a given kind or class of articles which are in excess of what is compatible with and commensurate to the person's normal requirements for personal use.

ai.title: Commercial Quantity
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Dami ng isang klase ng article na lampas sa normal na pangangailangan para sa personal use.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kung mas marami kaysa sa kailangan mo para sa sarili, 'commercial' na ang tingin dito.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ito ang batayan sa Secs. 4.1.2(b) at 4.2.3 tungkol sa vehicles at vessels na ginamit sa pagdadala ng smuggled goods.

paragraphs.text: Common Carrier — shall refer to persons, corporations, firms, or association engaged in the business of carrying or transporting passengers or goods or both, by land, water or air, for compensation, offering their services to the public.

ai.title: Common Carrier
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Tao, kumpanya o samahan na nagdadala ng pasahero o goods (land, water o air) kapalit ng bayad at bukas ang serbisyo sa publiko.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Halimbawa: bus company, shipping line, airline. Hindi ito private o pang-sarili lang.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Isa ito sa mga kundisyon sa Sec. 4.2.3 para hindi ma-forfeit ang conveyance.

paragraphs.text: Constructive Customs Custody — shall refer to the situation where, falling short of physical seizure or possession, the Customs Officers and the owner of the goods enter into a written agreement after the inventory to the effect that the goods, subject of a Letter of Authority (LOA), shall not be removed or disposed of pending disposition or resolution on the issue of whether proper payment of duties and taxes has been made.

ai.title: Constructive Customs Custody
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Written agreement ng Customs at ng owner pagkatapos ng inventory na hindi aalisin o idi-dispose ang goods habang hindi pa nareresolba kung tama ang bayad ng duties and taxes.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi physical na kinuha ang goods, pero 'hawak' pa rin ng Customs dahil sa kasunduan.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ginagamit ito sa Sec. 5.1 habang tumatakbo ang 15-day period.

paragraphs.text: Decision — shall refer to the disposition of the main forfeiture case by the District Collector or Commissioner based on merits.

ai.title: Decision
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Ang disposition ng main forfeiture case ng District Collector o Commissioner batay sa merits.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang aktuwal na ruling sa kaso, hindi ang mga incidental na orders.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Kaiba ito sa Interlocutory Order sa Sec. 3.15.

paragraphs.text: Decisions Adverse to the Government — shall refer to the disposition of the main forfeiture case based on merits, which resolves that there is no violation of the law that will warrant the Forfeiture of the seized articles, and consequently allows the release of the articles subject of a Warrant of Seizure and Detention (WSD) without payment of additional duties and taxes, interests, penalties and/or surcharges.

ai.title: Decisions Adverse to the Government
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Decision sa merits na walang violation na magpapa-forfeit sa seized articles, kaya puwedeng i-release ang goods nang walang dagdag na duties, taxes, interests, penalties o surcharges.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Panalo ito ng claimant. 'Adverse' dahil talo ang gobyerno.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ang ganitong Decision ang nagti-trigger ng automatic review ng Commissioner sa Sec. 17.

paragraphs.text: Deputized Officer — shall refer to officers or members of the Armed Forces of the Philippines (AFP) or other selected national law enforcement agencies covered by a written order signed by the Commissioner of Customs authorizing them to assist in the exercise of customs police authority, particularly the power to search, seize, and arrest in specified areas outside customs premises.

ai.title: Deputized Officer
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Mga officer o miyembro ng AFP o ibang piling national law enforcement agencies na may written order ng Commissioner para tumulong sa customs police authority (search, seize, arrest) sa specified areas sa labas ng customs premises.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Sila ang 'katuwang' ng Customs sa labas ng mga port. Puwede silang mag-serve ng WSD kasama ang ESS.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Kailangan ng written order na pirmado mismo ng Commissioner.

paragraphs.text: Free Carrier (FCA) — shall refer to an international commercial term covered by the Incoterms rules developed by International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) which means that the seller delivers the goods to the carrier or another person nominated by the buyer at the seller's premises or another named place.

ai.title: Free Carrier (FCA)
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Incoterm kung saan idinedeliver ng seller ang goods sa carrier o sa taong itinalaga ng buyer, sa premises ng seller o ibang named place.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ang delivery ay sa carrier o sa named place, hindi sa mismong barko.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: May silbi ang FCA value sa Sec. 17.2: Php 10,000,000.00 pataas ang nagpapa-akyat ng kaso sa Secretary of Finance.

paragraphs.text: Free on Board (FOB) — shall refer to international commercial term covered by the Incoterms rules developed by International Chamber of Commerce (ICC) which means that the seller delivers the goods on board the vessel nominated by the buyer at the named point of shipment, or procures the goods already delivered.

ai.title: Free on Board (FOB)
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Incoterm kung saan idinedeliver ng seller ang goods sa barkong itinalaga ng buyer sa named point of shipment, o kumukuha ng goods na naideliver na.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ang delivery ay 'on board' na ng vessel sa pinanggalingang port.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Kasama ang FOB value sa threshold ng Sec. 17.2 na Php 10,000,000.00 o higit pa.

paragraphs.text: Forfeiture — shall refer to the acquisition of ownership by the government for an established violation of CMTA as a result of the forfeiture proceedings.

ai.title: Forfeiture
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Pagkuha ng gobyerno ng ownership sa goods dahil sa established violation ng CMTA, bunga ng forfeiture proceedings.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Hindi sapat ang seizure. Ang forfeiture ang tunay na nagpapalipat ng ownership sa gobyerno.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Seizure = pagkuha o pag-hold sa goods. Forfeiture = pagkuha ng ownership.

paragraphs.text: Fraud — shall refer to acts knowingly, voluntarily and intentionally committed or omitted which prejudice the interest of the government, e.g. submitting fake or spurious document, making material untruthful statement(s) or committing any other analogous act(s) or omission(s).

ai.title: Fraud
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Mga kilos o pagkukulang na sinadya, kusa at may kaalaman na nakakasama sa interes ng gobyerno, gaya ng pag-submit ng pekeng document o material na hindi totoong statement.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Kailangan ng intensyon. Hindi ito simpleng pagkakamali o clerical error.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Kapag may Fraud, hindi puwede ang settlement by fine o redemption (Sec. 14.4.1).

paragraphs.text: Goods — shall refer to articles, wares, merchandise and any other items which are subject of importation or exportation.

ai.title: Goods
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Articles, wares, merchandise at iba pang items na subject ng importation o exportation.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Malawak ang saklaw: kahit anong dinadala papasok o palabas ng bansa.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ito ang pinakabatayang termino sa listahan ng Sec. 4.1.1.

paragraphs.text: Held Baggage Receipt (HBR) – shall refer to a receipt issued by a customs officer acknowledging that the baggage is temporarily held in custody by the Bureau for undeclared dutiable goods and/or declared dutiable goods pending payment of duties and taxes, verification of documents, or compliance with customs laws, rules and regulations.

ai.title: Held Baggage Receipt (HBR)
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Resibo na ibinibigay ng customs officer na pansamantalang hawak ng Bureau ang baggage dahil sa undeclared o declared dutiable goods na pending pa ang bayad, verification o compliance.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Parang claim stub sa baggage ng pasahero habang inaayos ang bayarin at documents.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ginagamit ang HBR sa Sec. 14.2 para sa undeclared dutiable goods ng arriving passenger.

paragraphs.text: Interlocutory Order — shall refer to the orders of the District Collector or Commissioner involving incidental matters that does not dispose of the case completely but leaves something to be decided upon.

ai.title: Interlocutory Order
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Orders ng District Collector o Commissioner sa incidental matters na hindi pa tuluyang nagdedesisyon sa kaso dahil may natitira pang dapat pagpasyahan.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: 'Pansamantalang' order lang ito, hindi ang final Decision.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ayon sa Sec. 14.1.3, ang order na nagde-deny ng Motion to Quash ay Interlocutory Order.

paragraphs.text: Landed Cost — shall refer to the sum of the customs value including the total cost of the product, transportation cost and insurance plus applicable customs duty and other taxable charges such as but not limited to brokerage fee, bank charge, other charges, processing fee, arrastre charges and wharfage dues, if applicable.

ai.title: Landed Cost
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Kabuuan ng customs value (kasama ang total cost ng product, transportation at insurance) dagdag ang customs duty at iba pang taxable charges tulad ng brokerage fee, bank charge, processing fee, arrastre at wharfage dues kung applicable.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Ito ang 'total na gastos' para mapunta ang goods sa Pilipinas.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Ito ang batayan ng 30% fine, 100% redemption (Sec. 14.4) at 30% surcharge sa undeclared baggage (Sec. 14.2).

paragraphs.text: Misclassification — shall refer to the use of insufficient or wrong description of the goods or the use of erroneous tariff heading/s and sub-heading/s resulting in deficiency between the duty and tax that should have been paid and the duty and tax actually paid; and/or to avoid compliance with government regulations related to the entry of Regulated, Prohibited or Restricted goods into Philippine Customs territory.

ai.title: Misclassification
ai.content:
📖 Kahulugan: Paggamit ng kulang o maling description ng goods, o maling tariff heading at sub-heading, na nagresulta sa kulang na duty and tax; o para iwasan ang regulasyon sa Regulated, Prohibited o Restricted goods.

💡 Simpleng Paliwanag: Maling 'classification' ng goods, halimbawa maling tariff heading. May kakulangan sa binayarang duty and tax o umiwas sa regulasyon.

⚠️ Dapat Tandaan: Kaiba ito sa Misdeclaration. Ang Misclassification ay tungkol sa maling description o tariff heading.
ai.prompt: Ipaliwanag nang simple ang Sec. 3.17 ng CAO No. 10-2020 tungkol sa Misclassification. Magbigay ng practical customs example, ipaliwanag kung bakit ito umiiral, banggitin ang related provisions, at linawin ang common misconceptions.

paragraphs.text: Misdeclaration — shall refer to a false, untruthful, erroneous or inaccurate declaration as to quantity, quality, description, weight or measurement of the goods resulting in deficiency between the duty and tax that should have been paid and the duty and tax actually paid; and/or to avoid compliance with government regulations related to the entry of Regulated, Prohibited or Restricted goods into Philippine customs territory.

ai.title: Misdeclaration
